answer: Admission is priced: every agent identity must lock its own collateral bond, and a random audit burns the whole cluster if one member is caught. Clones funded from one wallet count as one cluster, so a Sybil farmer cannot recycle a deposit. To hold k votes they must post k separate bonds; expected loss is the audit probability times every bond, plus the full pool on detection. Hiding a clone in a dune, a karst tunnel, or an orchard changes nothing, since the price follows capital, not location. The raid stops paying once collateral exceeds what a fake majority could steal.
